newsitem.title: USA: Economists sign statement opposing Dole tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Economists sign statement opposing Dole tax plan.

text.p: Hundreds of economists opposed Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole's tax cut proposal, saying it would increase the budget deficit, the Economic Policy Institute said on Tuesday.
Dole has proposed $548 billion in tax relief measures including a 15 percent reduction in personal income tax rates.

"Such tax cuts would divert resources to consumption and raise the federal deficit, ultimately diminishing the capital available for public and private productive investments," the statement signed by 546 economists said.
"The result would be a lowering of future living standards," the statement said.

The majority of economists were from universities, with a handful from labour unions and the World Bank. The signatories included seven Nobel laureates and former Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Alan Blinder.
The Economic Policy Institute, a liberal non-profit think tank, released the statement.
Meanwhile, CapitolWatch, a conservative non-profit lobbying group, endorsed Dole's tax proposal saying cutting government waste could pay for it.

Billions of dollars could be saved by "cutting corporate welfare and downsizing the government bureaucracy -- by consolidating agencies and elimnating whole cabinet departments that have long outlived their usefulness," Beau Boulter, chairman of CapitolWatch, said in a statement.

"Bob Dole's tax cut is a necessity if this nation is going to provide jobs, opportunity and economic growth in the aftermath of (President) Bill Clinton's status quo stagnation and Dole can do it by targeting wasteful spending," he said.
